title: Thalia dealbata

{{Short description|Species of aquatic plant}} {{Speciesbox | image = Thalia dealbata CF2P6836.jpg | genus = Thalia | species = dealbata | authority = [[John Fraser (botanist)|Fraser]] ex Roscoe | synonyms = *''Malacarya dealbata'' (Fraser) Raf. *''Maranta dealbata'' (Fraser) A.Dietr. *''Peronia stricta'' F.Delaroche *''Spirostalis biflora'' Raf. *''Spirostylis biflora'' Raf. *''Thalia barbata'' Small | synonyms_ref = [http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-268123 The Plant List, ''Thalia dealbata''] }} {{Commons category}} '''''Thalia dealbata''''', the '''powdery alligator-flag''',{{PLANTS|id=THDE|taxon=Thalia dealbata|accessdate=9 December 2015}} '''hardy canna''', or '''powdery thalia''', is an [[aquatic plant]] in the family [[Marantaceae]], native to swamps, ponds and other wetlands in the southern and central [[United States]].[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/766823#page/368/mode/1up Roscoe, William. 1807. Transactions of the Linnean Society of London 8: 340, ''Thalia dealbata'' ][https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7430545#page/405/mode/1up Rafinesque, Constantine Samuel. 1838. Flora Telluriana 4: 51. ''Spirostylis biflora''] Its range includes much of Coastal Plains and the lower [[Mississippi Valley]] (States of [[South Carolina]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[Alabama]], [[Mississippi]], [[Louisiana]], [[Texas]], [[Oklahoma]], [[Arkansas]], [[Missouri]], [[Illinois]] and [[Kentucky]]).[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Thalia%20dealbata.png Biota of North America Program, 2014 county distribution map, ''Thalia dealbata''] The plant has been grown as an aquatic ornamental because of the pretty violet flowers, and in cultivation has been proved hardy as far north as [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania|Philadelphia]] ([[Pennsylvania]]) and [[Vancouver, British Columbia|Vancouver]] ([[British Columbia]]).[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000385 Flora of North America ''Thalia dealbata''][https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=THDE United States Department of Agriculture Plants Profile][http://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=thde Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center, University of Texas, Native Plant Database] ''Thalia dealbata'' grows to {{convert|6|ft|m|abbr=on}}, with small violet flowers on an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} panicle held above the foliage. The blue-green leaves are [[Leaf shape|ovate to lanceolate]], dusted with white powder and with purple edges.{{cite web|url=http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/water-garden/marginalaq/thalia_dealbata.html|title=Marginal Aquatics: Thalia dealbata|last=Evans|first=Erv|publisher=North Carolina State University|accessdate=15 May 2010|archive-date=19 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100719130045/http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/water-garden/marginalaq/thalia_dealbata.html|url-status=dead}}[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/a646/thalia-dealbata.aspx Missouri Botanical Garden] ==Gallery== Thalia dealbata MHNT.BOT.2013.22.62.jpg|''Thalia dealbata''
